Untapping Jor Kadeen would give them a 5/4 first strike blocker, which is valuable defensively.
annotations.actionTaken: Selected Osgir, the Reconstructor as the untap target for Thousand-Year Elixir

annotations.description: GPT5m Spike sacrificed Sol Ring, their best mana rock that produces 2 colorless mana per tap, instead of Boros Locket which is a slower, less efficient mana rock (produces only 1 mana per tap). Sol Ring is one of the most powerful mana acceleration cards in the format and sacrificing it over a Boros Locket is a massive loss of mana efficiency. The context appears to be some forced sacrifice effect, but choosing Sol Ring over Boros Locket or even Thousand-Year Elixir (which has limited utility with only Jor Kadeen on board) is clearly wrong.
annotations.actionTaken: Sacrificed Sol Ring to whatever effect required an artifact sacrifice
annotations.betterLine: Sacrifice Boros Locket instead, preserving Sol Ring's superior mana production. Boros Locket only taps for 1 mana versus Sol Ring's 2, making it the clearly inferior artifact to keep.

annotations.description: GPT5m Spike sacrificed Boros Locket to Osgir's ability to give Jor Kadeen +2/+0, but Jor Kadeen is already tapped (presumably from attacking or some previous activation). The +2/+0 boost during precombat main is wasted if Jor Kadeen already attacked. More importantly, sacrificing Boros Locket removes a mana rock that produces R or W and could later be sacrificed for card draw. Thousand-Year Elixir would have been a better sacrifice choice since Osgir is already tapped and the Elixir's untap ability is less critical. However, the real issue is that Boros Locket has significant value - it's a mana source and a potential card draw engine. Additionally, Osgir can later exile artifacts from the graveyard to create token copies, so sacrificing Boros Locket does put it in the graveyard for potential future use with Osgir's second ability (exile to make two copies). But the timing is questionable - pumping an already-tapped creature during precombat main seems to accomplish nothing this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Sacrificed Boros Locket to Osgir to give the already-tapped Jor Kadeen +2/+0 during precombat main.
annotations.betterLine: If the goal was to set up Boros Locket in the graveyard for Osgir's token-copying ability, wait until it's more impactful. If pumping was needed, sacrifice Thousand-Year Elixir instead since it provides less ongoing value with Osgir already being used. Alternatively, hold the sacrifice for when it matters in combat.

This would have provided massive mana acceleration AND activated metalcraft (3 artifacts) for Jor Kadeen, giving all creatures +3/+0.
annotations.actionTaken: Used Thousand-Year Elixir to untap Jor Kadeen, the Prevailer, who can only attack as a 5/4 without metalcraft.
annotations.betterLine: Use Thousand-Year Elixir to untap Osgir, then pay {1} to exile Sol Ring from graveyard with Osgir's ability, creating two Sol Ring tokens. This provides +4 mana per turn and enables metalcraft for Jor Kadeen's +3/+0 buff to all creatures.

annotations.description: The player's reasoning references a '51/51 Serra Avatar' on Sonnet Villain's board, but no such creature exists - Sonnet only has Serene Master (0/2). Casting Peel from Reality here would bounce their own Ramunap Excavator (which is providing graveyard land recursion value with Terramorphic Expanse in graveyard) just to bounce a 0/2 Serene Master - a terrible exchange based on a completely incorrect threat assessment.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Peel from Reality to bounce a nonexistent Serra Avatar, actually bouncing Serene Master (0/2) while losing their own Ramunap Excavator from the battlefield.
annotations.betterLine: Neither spell needed to be cast during their own combat. If forced to choose, Beast Within could at least be saved for a real threat. Ideally, pass without casting either reactive spell and continue developing the board toward Stormtide Leviathan or Scourge of Fleets.

annotations.description: Playing Forest as the land drop instead of casting Ramunap Excavator first and then using the land drop to play Terramorphic Expanse from the graveyard. By playing Forest first, they use their land drop on a basic rather than getting the Terramorphic Expanse into play (which can be cracked for additional deck thinning and fixing). They can still cast Excavator after Forest, but then the Terramorphic Expanse play is delayed a turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Forest from hand as their land drop
annotations.betterLine: Cast Ramunap Excavator (2G with 3 untapped mana), then play Terramorphic Expanse from graveyard as land drop, crack it to fetch a basic land - getting the same board development but a turn faster on graveyard land recursion value.

annotations.description: Kimi25 Gramps has 6 lands (4 untapped: Island, Forest, Island, Forest) and Ramunap Excavator costs only 2G. Playing Ramunap Excavator would establish a 2/3 body and enable replaying Terramorphic Expanse from the graveyard, accelerating future land drops and fixing. There's no reason to hold it - it's a value creature that gets better the earlier it's played. The player has Terramorphic Expanse in the graveyard ready to replay. Holding up mana for Beast Within or Whelming Wave isn't necessary here since there are no immediate threats requiring answers - Whelming Wave is a sorcery anyway and can't be cast at instant speed.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting anything, keeping mana open.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Ramunap Excavator (2G) to start replaying Terramorphic Expanse from the graveyard for extra land drops and deck thinning. Still leaves 1 mana open, and Beast Within could be held for a future turn when there's an actual threat to answer.

annotations.description: Casting Serra Avatar (a 53/53) for 7 mana is powerful but risky. With 7 mana available, Serra Avatar costs all of it, leaving no mana open for protection. The board has multiple opponents who could answer it (Kimi25 has Beast Within in their colors, bounce spells in graveyard). Additionally, casting a creature before combat when you have no attackers anyway is fine sequencing-wise, but the bigger question is whether Tower Gargoyle (4/4 flyer for 4 mana) + Vizkopa Guildmage (2 mana) would have been a better split, leaving up mana and deploying multiple threats that are harder to answer with a single removal spell. However, a 53/53 is extremely threatening and demands an immediate answer, so this is defensible.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Serra Avatar as a 53/53 for 7 mana, using all available mana
annotations.betterLine: Could have cast Tower Gargoyle (4 mana) + Vizkopa Guildmage (2 mana) to deploy two threats while keeping 1 mana open, or cast Tower Gargoyle + Augury Adept to build board presence more resiliently. Serra Avatar is high-risk since a single bounce or removal undoes the entire turn.

annotations.description: Whelming Wave bounces all creatures except Krakens, Leviathans, Octopuses, and Serpents. Serra Avatar (an Avatar) gets bounced, which is good. However, Kimi25 has Stormtide Leviathan in hand (a Leviathan, exempt from Whelming Wave) and Scourge of Fleets (a Kraken, also exempt). Playing Whelming Wave now for 4 mana leaves only 3 mana remaining - not enough to cast Stormtide Leviathan (8 mana) or Scourge of Fleets (7 mana) this turn. If Kimi25 had waited one more turn to accumulate 8 mana (with the Island in hand as a land drop), they could have cast Whelming Wave + followed up with a threat next turn at 8+ mana, or even cast Stormtide Leviathan directly. The issue is that bouncing Serra Avatar without being able to deploy a finisher means Sonnet Villain can simply replay it. That said, the Serra Avatar is a 53/53 that threatens lethal, so removing it immediately has urgency. Beast Within could have destroyed it permanently (leaving only a 3/3 token) while preserving the Whelming Wave for a bigger swing turn with Stormtide Leviathan or Scourge of Fleets.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Whelming Wave to bounce all non-Kraken/Leviathan/Octopus/Serpent creatures, including the 53/53 Serra Avatar.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Beast Within targeting Serra Avatar to permanently destroy it (Serra Avatar shuffles into library from graveyard, but the controller gets only a 3/3 Beast token). This preserves Whelming Wave for a future turn where it can be paired with Stormtide Leviathan or Scourge of Fleets for a devastating board-clearing + threat deployment turn.

annotations.description: GPT5m Spike used Duplicant's imprint ETB trigger to exile its own Duplicant instead of exiling the opponent's Ramunap Excavator. Duplicant's imprint ability says 'you may exile target nontoken creature' — exiling itself removes your own creature for no benefit (it just exiles itself and ceases to exist as a 2/4 body). Ramunap Excavator is the only opposing creature on the board, and it enables Kimi25 Gramps to replay lands from graveyard (including Terramorphic Expanse for repeated value). Exiling it would remove that engine and leave GPT5m Spike with a creature on board that copies the Excavator's stats.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to exile their own Duplicant with Duplicant's imprint trigger, effectively destroying their own creature for nothing.
annotations.betterLine: Exile Ramunap Excavator with Duplicant's imprint ability, removing the opponent's graveyard-land engine and keeping a creature on the battlefield.

annotations.description: Casting Stormtide Leviathan while holding Beast Within is defensible but questionable. Serra Avatar is a 55/55 that threatens lethal damage, and Stormtide Leviathan does prevent it from attacking (no flying/islandwalk). However, Beast Within could destroy Serra Avatar directly right now for 3 mana, turning a 55/55 into a 3/3 Beast. The Leviathan costs 8 mana (all of Kimi's mana), leaving nothing up for interaction. Additionally, Stormtide Leviathan makes all lands Islands, which could enable Sonnet Villain to recast Oloro more easily with the mana fixing, and it shuts down Kimi's own Ramunap Excavator from attacking. That said, Stormtide Leviathan is an 8/8 with islandwalk that can attack through any opponent with Islands (which is everyone once it's out), and it protects against ground-based threats from all opponents. The play has clear strategic merit as a win condition that also stops Serra Avatar, but using Beast Within on Serra Avatar first and saving the Leviathan for next turn (playing the Island from hand first) could have been considered.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Stormtide Leviathan for 8 mana, using all available mana
annotations.betterLine: Play Island from hand first, then cast Beast Within targeting Serra Avatar (removing the biggest threat immediately for 3 mana), keeping Stormtide Leviathan for next turn when you'd have 8+ mana with the extra Island. This removes the 55/55 threat immediately while preserving options.

annotations.description: Fetched Forest when the hand is heavily blue-leaning. Most castable spells need U (Whispering Madness needs UB, Aeon Chronicler needs UU, Etherium-Horn Sorcerer needs UR, Coiling Oracle needs GU). Opulent Palace already provides G, so a second green source is redundant while a second blue source would better enable the hand's key spells.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched Forest from Terramorphic Expanse
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Island to better support the blue-heavy hand (Whispering Madness, Aeon Chronicler, Etherium-Horn Sorcerer all need blue mana)

annotations.description: Whispering Madness costs {2}{U}{B} and forces each player to discard their hand and draw cards equal to the greatest number discarded. Llama4 Stoic has 6 cards in hand (including Whispering Madness itself, so 5 after casting). This symmetric effect helps opponents as much or more than it helps Llama4. Sonnet Villain at 57 life with Serra Avatar is the clear threat, and giving them a fresh hand of cards is dangerous. Meanwhile, Llama4 is discarding strong cards like Army of the Damned, Aeon Chronicler, and Etherium-Horn Sorcerer for random draws. Horizon Chimera (flash, flying, trample, gains life on draw) or Coiling Oracle would have been much better plays - developing the board while keeping the strong cards in hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Whispering Madness, discarding their entire hand including Army of the Damned, Aeon Chronicler, and Etherium-Horn Sorcerer to give all players fresh cards.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Coiling Oracle to develop the board and potentially hit a land drop, or cast Horizon Chimera as a flash flyer that gains incremental life. Save Whispering Madness for when you have fewer cards or can encode it on a creature for repeated value.

annotations.description: Serra Avatar (59/59) has no trample or evasion. GPT5m Spike has Digsite Engineer (3/3) which can chump block, preventing all combat damage to the player. Meanwhile, Llama4 Stoic has zero creatures on the battlefield and would die to 59 unblocked damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked GPT5m Spike with Serra Avatar, who has a creature that can chump block the non-evasive Avatar.
annotations.betterLine: Attack Llama4 Stoic with Serra Avatar for a guaranteed kill, since Stoic has no creatures to block.

annotations.description: Llama4 Stoic is in a 1v1 situation against Sonnet Villain who has 61 life and a Serra Avatar on board (which likely has power/toughness equal to Sonnet's life total = 61/61). Casting Yidris (5/4 trample) into a 61/61 Serra Avatar is extremely dangerous - Yidris needs to connect with a player to get value from cascade, and Serra Avatar dominates the board. Meanwhile, Llama4 has Horizon Chimera (3/2 flying, trample) which could actually fly over Serra Avatar and start dealing damage while providing life gain on card draws. The reasoning mentions playing 'Drowned Catacomb' but then casts Yidris instead, suggesting confused decision-making. Horizon Chimera for 4 mana would be a much better play - it has evasion to get past Serra Avatar, and its flash means it could have been held up. Additionally, Coiling Oracle (2 mana) into Thrasios (2 mana) would develop the board more efficiently, or Coiling Oracle + Horizon Chimera could be cast together for 6 mana total.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Yidris, Maelstrom Wielder (4 mana, 5/4 trample) from command zone, which likely costs extra due to commander tax and cannot profitably attack into a 61/61 Serra Avatar.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Horizon Chimera (3/2 flying, trample) which can fly over Serra Avatar to deal damage and provide incremental life gain, possibly alongside Coiling Oracle for card/mana advantage. Flying evasion is critical when facing a massive ground blocker like Serra Avatar.

annotations.description: Casting Phyrexian Gargantua before combat when Serra Avatar already represents lethal damage against the only remaining opponent (41 life). The Gargantua also loses 2 life (not gains, as the reasoning incorrectly states), shrinking Serra Avatar from 63/63 to 61/61, though this doesn't affect the lethal math. Casting spells pre-combat when you have lethal on board is poor sequencing.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Phyrexian Gargantua (losing 2 life, drawing 2 cards) before attacking with a lethal Serra Avatar
annotations.betterLine: Attack immediately with Serra Avatar for lethal. Yidris can block but trample ensures 58+ damage gets through against 41 life. Cast any additional spells in second main phase only if needed.

annotations.description: Tapped Opulent Palace (which produces 3 colors) for {G} instead of tapping the mono-colored Forest for {G}. This leaves the less flexible Forest untapped instead of the more versatile Opulent Palace, reducing options for any remaining plays this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Tapped Opulent Palace for {G} to help cast Horizon Chimera
annotations.betterLine: Tap Forest for {G} instead, keeping the more flexible Opulent Palace untapped for potential additional plays

annotations.description: Sonnet Villain has a 71-life Serra Avatar (71/71) on the battlefield and is about to attack. With Vizkopa Guildmage's second ability ({1}{W}{B}: Whenever you gain life this turn, each opponent loses that much life), giving Serra Avatar lifelink would mean dealing 71 combat damage, gaining 71 life, and then each opponent losing 71 life - which would kill the remaining opponent Llama4 Stoic at 41 life. Instead, they chose the first ability (just lifelink) without activating the second ability first, missing the lethal combo.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Vizkopa Guildmage's first ability (give lifelink) without first activating the second ability (life gain causes opponents to lose that much life).
annotations.betterLine: Activate Vizkopa Guildmage's second ability first ({1}{W}{B}: Whenever you gain life this turn, each opponent loses that much life), THEN activate the first ability to give Serra Avatar lifelink. Attack with Serra Avatar for 71 damage, gain 71 life, and Llama4 Stoic loses 71 life from the triggered ability - lethal on the only remaining opponent.
